results.controlIntent: a. Use internal system clocks to produce time stamps for audit records; and b. Record, for audit records, those time stamps meeting [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] that satisfy one or more of the following: use Coordinated Universal Time; have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time; include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: Both CloudTrail audit records retrieved for the churn-predictor-endpoint use timestamps in ISO 8601 format with UTC (Zulu, "Z" suffix): CreateEndpoint at 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z (evidence aee44a6b) and UpdateEndpoint at 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z (evidence c83e4e20). AWS CloudTrail inherently uses internal AWS system clocks (satisfying AU-8.r3a) and records all event times in Coordinated Universal Time at second-level granularity (satisfying AU-8.r3b). The timestamps are substantive — they are unambiguous, UTC-anchored, and granular to the second — meeting the control's adequacy standard. No evidence of non-UTC or missing timestamps was found in the retrieved records.
gaps: Organization-defined granularity requirement (e.g., millisecond vs. second) was not explicitly documented in retrieved evidence — human attestation of the organization's defined granularity standard would strengthen this assessment.
Only two CloudTrail events were retrieved; a broader sample across all endpoint lifecycle events (e.g., DeleteEndpoint, model registry approvals) would provide more comprehensive coverage.
No direct evidence of NTP/time-sync configuration for the underlying infrastructure was retrieved — AWS manages this internally, but explicit documentation would be ideal for a full audit.
